charts.title: Cash vs Total Debt vs Net Bank Debt

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Seeka Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted); net bank debt is the company-reported covenant measure (bank debt less cash).

For Seeka Limited: net bank debt fell from a $172m 2023 peak to $119.8m at June 2026, with the leverage ratio improving to 1.22x from 1.60x a year earlier -- the deleveraging the company credits for its banking syndicate renewal and return to a twice-yearly dividend. It is seasonal: debt builds through H1 to fund harvest working capital, then falls as receivables are collected from Zespri in H2.

What to watch:

  • June (H1) readings are seasonally elevated -- compare against the prior June, not the prior December
  • Net bank debt trend versus EBITDA and covenant headroom

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Seeka Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Seeka Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Seeka Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Seeka Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Seeka Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Seeka Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

trays.title: Kiwifruit volume
trays.content:
Trays grown is the gross NZ kiwifruit crop on orchards Seeka services; trays packed is what the post-harvest business actually processes, split into Class 1 (export-grade) and the SunGold variety within it.

For Seeka Limited: post-harvest fee revenue is earned per tray packed, so this is the segment's volume driver -- H1 FY2026 NZ Class 1 volume fell 4% (Hayward down 13% on lower yields) while SunGold still grew 2% to a record 30.4m trays, and EBITDA rose anyway on automation efficiency, the operating-leverage story the qualitative analysis flags.

What to watch:

  • SunGold's growing share of total packed volume (higher per-tray economics than Hayward)
  • Trays grown vs trays packed Class 1 -- the gap is crop downgraded below export grade
  • Data is interim-only (H1) where management discloses it mid-season; a blank FY bar is not a missing year

yield.title: Orchard yield per hectare
yield.content:
Yield per hectare (trays/ha) measures orchard productivity, reported separately for the SunGold and Hayward (green) varieties Seeka grows and manages.

For Seeka Limited: yield is weather-driven and the main swing factor in Orcharding segment profit -- H1 FY2026 Hayward yield fell to 10,055 trays/ha from 12,332 a year earlier, and Orcharding EBIT fell 20% as a result, even as post-harvest EBIT still grew on the volume it did process.

What to watch:

  • SunGold yield consistently well above Hayward (reflects the variety's higher-value conversion economics)
  • Multi-year yield trend as a read on orchard age, growing conditions and climate risk (frost, cyclones)

postHarvest.title: Post-harvest segment revenue and EBIT
postHarvest.content:
Post-harvest revenue and EBIT isolate Seeka's core packing and coolstorage business -- fee-for-service income from independent growers -- from Orcharding, SeekaFresh retail and the Australian operations reported alongside it.

For Seeka Limited: this is the segment management credits for the FY2024-26 recovery: Reemoon packhouse automation lifted margins even as H1 FY2026 NZ tray volumes fell 4%, with post-harvest EBIT still up 7% to $73.3m.

What to watch:

  • EBIT margin (EBIT / revenue) trend as automation capex is absorbed
  • Whether post-harvest growth is offsetting weaker Orcharding or Australia results in the group total

leaseRecon.title: IFRS-16 lease reconciliation
leaseRecon.content:
EBITDA (pre-IFRS 16) is the covenant-basis measure Seeka's banking syndicate uses, before the IFRS-16 lease depreciation and interest that reported EBITDA already excludes are added back on top; the two lease lines show the IFRS-16 charge's split between depreciation and imputed interest.

For Seeka Limited: most of Seeka's orchards are leased rather than owned, so the IFRS-16 lease charge is large relative to earnings; the pre-IFRS-16 figure is what the leverage covenant (1.22x at June 2026) is actually measured against, not statutory EBITDA.

What to watch:

  • Gap between reported and pre-IFRS-16 EBITDA widening as more orchards are leased rather than owned
  • Lease interest expense trend alongside bank interest as a full financing-cost picture

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Seeka Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Seeka Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
